title: Internal Hom base change through a filtered finite-free coefficient colimit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with a sheaf of commutative rings $R$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], relative derived tensor computed using K-flat complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Assume filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of sheaves of commutative $R$-algebras, with each $S_i$ isomorphic as an $R$-module sheaf to $R^{d_i}$ for a finite nonnegative integer $d_i$. Let $S=\varinjlim_i S_i$ be its sheaf-algebra colimit, whose underlying module is the filtered sheaf-module colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $K\in D(R)$ satisfy the following continuity property: for every diagram $(M_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ of cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with a common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced map
$$\varinjlim_i H_R(K,M_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R(K,\varinjlim_i M_i^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism, with filtered colimits computed by exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial representatives. For every $L\in D(R)$ with bounded-below cohomology, the canonical evaluation-transpose comparison
$$S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. It is natural in $K,L$ and in compatible morphisms of the algebra diagrams. Its restriction to $D(R)$, under the evaluation-normalized scalar-adjunction identification, is the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)&\simeq\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes_R H_R(K,L))\\
&\simeq\varinjlim_i H_R(K,S_i\otimes_R L)\\
&\simeq H_R(K,S\otimes_R L).
\end{aligned}$$
In this formula a bounded-below representative of $L$ is used, and the stage comparisons are the evaluation-defined ones. They are compatible with every transition map of the diagram, independently of choices of finite bases. No constructibility of $L$ or finite Tor amplitude of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a representative D of L with cohomology zero below b. Its good lower truncation C has $D^b/\operatorname{im}d^{b-1}$ in degree b and zero terms below b; $D\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the cohomology formula. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative P of K. Put $J=I_R(C)$, $B=\mathcal Hom(P,J)$ and $F=\operatorname{homFixed}(P)$ in the strict models. The one-K-flat transpose lemma identifies the evaluation transposes used below with chain evaluation, without assuming B K-flat.

proof.text: Tensor-colimit preservation gives $S\otimes A=\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes A)$. Each stage functor is $A\mapsto A^{d_i}$ and is exact; the assumed exact filtered colimit makes $S\otimes-$ exact. Exact functors commute with cohomology, so these tensors compute derived scalar extension and exact termwise colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the normalized transformation $a_T$ and roof denominator $v_T$ of the strict roof. The finite-free-stage node makes every $a_{S_i},v_{S_i}$ a quasi-isomorphism. The continuity node supplies $v_S$, $\lambda_J:\varinjlim_iF(S_i\otimes J)\to F(S\otimes J)$ and the tensor cocone isomorphism. Its hypotheses hold since $S_i\otimes C$ all vanish below $b$ and the stated continuity hypothesis is Continuous(P) on these representatives.

proof.text: Put $a=\varinjlim a_{S_i}$, $v=\varinjlim v_{S_i}$ and let $\lambda_C$ be the continuity map. Exact colimits make $a,v$ quasi-isomorphisms. Strict naturality and the colimit universal property give $\lambda_Ja=a_S$ and $\lambda_Jv=v_S\lambda_C$ on complexes. Thus $\gamma=[\lambda_C][v]^{-1}[a]$ is an isomorphism and $[v_S]\gamma=[a_S]$. This is exactly the three-arrow formula, with its middle arrow the colimit roof.

proof.text: The flat-evaluation-roof node identifies $\Theta U(c)=[v_S]^{-1}[a_S]=\gamma$. Since $\Theta$ is invertible and $U$ conservative, $c$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. The roof identification also identifies each stage map with evaluation, independently of finite bases.

The strict scalar square and uniqueness of the normalized transformation make all the cocone identities natural. Therefore the formula and $c$ have every stated naturality; inverses of these natural isomorphisms are natural too.

This is the human-ordered re-split: the statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live, and the proof is now 2269 characters. The assembly is correct. Exactness of S⊗− comes from finite-free stages and exact colimits. The filtered-continuity hypotheses hold (C bounded below; Continuous(P) is the item's hypothesis and does not depend on the representative). The chain equations λ_J a = a_S (modulo the tensor-cocone iso (iii)) and λ_J v = v_S λ_C give [v_S]γ = [a_S] before localization. The roof node gives ΘU(c) = γ, and conservative U makes c an iso. I checked the three new statement-only nodes and all are true. The one-K-flat transpose holds because tensoring with K-flat P preserves quasi-isos and ev is a chain map. The scalar chain identification holds: θ(g)(x) = g(1⊗x) on slices, σ_q is balanced and unique, and the strict square sends s⊗f to s·q(1⊗f(x)). For the evaluation roof, both transposes are (s⊗f)⊗p ↦ s⊗f(p); for R = S it reduces to η_J ≃ I(η_C), which holds. None restates an item clause, and none duplicates an existing node: def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model and kflat-rhom-currying need both factors K-flat, and the ordinary adjunction node gives Hom-sets only. No cycle. I accept the 3 declared tool_uses (kflat-resolution, derived-change-of-rings, independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits). FIX (B2): the roof node used Q and U without introducing them.
